memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "I will accept nothing but what my men have eaten and the share that belongs to the men who went with me - to Aner, Eshkol and Mamre. Let them have their share." - Gen 14:24 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Abram refuses the spoils for himself - but notice he does not impose that refusal on everyone else. His allies Aner, Eshkol, and Mamre had fought alongside him, and Abram insists they receive their fair share. His convictions bound his own conscience, not theirs.

This is a beautiful mark of maturity. Abram held a strong personal conviction and lived it costly. But he did not become self-righteous about it, nor did he force it on others or shame them for not sharing it. He simply said: this is what I must do; let them have theirs.

We often struggle here. Once we take a stand, we can slide into judging everyone who hasn't taken the same one. Our personal convictions harden into rules for others, and we mistake our preferences for God's commands.

Paul addressed this exact tension: "One person considers one day more sacred than another; another considers every day alike. Each of them should be fully convinced in their own mind... Who are you to judge someone else's servant?" (Rom 14:5,4). Hold your convictions firmly for yourself, and hold others generously. Abram refused a fortune and made sure his friends were paid. That is principle without pride.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Do your personal convictions ever harden into judgement of others?
- Can you hold a firm stand for yourself while being generous with others?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, give me convictions I hold firmly and a heart that holds others generously. Keep me from turning my personal stands into judgement of my brothers and sisters.
Amen.
